routing.explain.body_1: Every site or app you open sends requests, one per address. At this point a request has no color yet: nothing has decided where it goes.
routing.explain.body_2: A Clash-style client takes the request over through the system proxy or TUN. All it knows is the domain or IP the request is going to.
routing.explain.body_3: Rules are checked from the first one down. The first rule that recognizes the request wins and the rest are skipped. That is the moment the request gets its color. The last rule is the final catch-all for anything not recognized above.
routing.explain.body_4: A rule only says which proxy group handles the request. The group then picks a member: chosen by hand, the lowest latency, the next one when one fails, or spread across several. A member can be another group; until you choose by hand, each layer uses its first member.
routing.explain.body_5: Purple leaves through a proxy node, teal goes direct over your own network, and the dashed orange line is blocked on your device and never sent.
routing.explain.figure: A request passes through the app, the client, the rules and the proxy groups, then leaves through a proxy node, goes direct or is blocked
routing.explain.title: How traffic flows

routing.lint.http_probe: The test URL uses HTTP; some networks hijack HTTP tests, so HTTPS is recommended.
routing.lint.latency_only: Only the latency of the latest test is compared; bandwidth and packet loss are not.
routing.lint.lazy_stale: No tests while idle (lazy, on by default in mihomo): the first connection after a long idle period uses old test results.
routing.lint.round_robin: “Round robin” sends one site's connections through different exits, which tends to break sign-ins and trigger risk checks.
routing.lint.single_member: Only one member, so automatic selection does nothing.
routing.lint.tolerance_zero: Tolerance is 0: whichever member was faster in the latest test wins, so a few milliseconds cause switching and the exit IP changes. 50–100 ms is common.

routing.type_info.fallback_avoid: It does not switch away from a first choice that connects but is slow: it only checks whether it connects.
routing.type_info.fallback_fit: A clear order of preference plus availability: stays on the first choice and switches only when it fails.
routing.type_info.fallback_tip: Uses the first available member in order and moves to the next when it is down.
routing.type_info.load-balance_avoid: Sites that keep you signed in: “round robin” sends one site's connections through different exits.
routing.type_info.load-balance_fit: Heavy multi-connection downloads that do not care about the exit IP; use “by destination”.
routing.type_info.select_avoid: It does not switch when a node fails; you switch by hand.
routing.type_info.select_fit: Services that care about your exit IP (AI, streaming, banking): one fixed node that is never switched automatically.
routing.type_info.select_tip: You pick a member in the client; until you do, the first one is used.
routing.type_info.url-test_avoid: AI, streaming and other IP-sensitive services: test jitter moves the exit between nodes.
routing.type_info.url-test_fit: General browsing and downloads that do not care about the exit IP; best with nodes from one region.
routing.type_info.url-test_tip: Tests latency periodically and uses the member with the lowest latency in the latest test; it does not switch while the gap is within the tolerance.

rules.hosts_hint: Addresses must come from public code hosts and their CDNs; paste the text for anything else. Allowed sites:
rules.order_hint: Drag the handle on the left to reorder; the order is saved to your account and also used in the wizard and configs.
rules.reorder: Drag to reorder: {name} (arrow keys when focused)
rules.subtitle: Proxy groups and routing rules; a config picks one under Nodes & routing.
rules.text_hint: Leave empty to use the URL above
rules.title: Routing rules
rules.via_hint: Both can be added later on the detail page; when a file has both pasted text and a URL, the pasted text wins.
settings.auto_add: Add received nodes to Nodes automatically
settings.auto_add_hint: They are not used in any config until you choose to; when off, add them from the message.
settings.auto_check_hint: After each autosave, the mihomo core checks that the config loads; the result shows in the top bar.
settings.field_click_hint.card: Any blank part of the card works; inputs, switches, buttons and links behave as usual.
settings.field_click_hint.text: Click the field name or the one-line description under it.
settings.inbox_hint: When off, nobody can message you; senders only see “recipient not found or not accepting messages”.
settings.motion_off_hint: Turns off animations and transitions. The indicator only shows on or off. Motion is already reduced when your system asks for it.
settings.subtitle: These only affect how the site looks and works for you. Sign-in security is under Account & security; site-wide options are under Admin.
settings.tz_hint: Type any part of a city or region, such as shanghai, tokyo or +8. Saved to your account, so it is the same on every device; times on these pages use it, and so does the header of generated configs that don't set their own time zone.
setup.done: The administrator already exists. Please sign in.
setup.subtitle: No accounts yet. Create the administrator here.
setup.title: Initial setup
share.template_hint: They get a copy of this template to edit freely. It references your nodes, which are skipped when they create a config from it.
short.code_random: Leave empty for a random code
short.delete_confirm: Delete /u/{code}? Clients using it will stop updating.
short.no_links: No config links yet. Create one on a config’s Config links page first.
short.received_hint: Copy or import into a client. They stop working if the owner revokes them.
short.safety: Anyone with a short link can download this config. Random codes can’t be guessed; custom codes are memorable but easier to guess. Repeated wrong guesses from one IP are rate-limited.
short.subtitle: Turn config links into short, memorable addresses. Opening one returns the config, and each request counts in Analytics.
source.client_fetch: Clients update this subscription themselves, so its nodes aren’t shown here.
source.content_hint: Share links (one per line), base64 subscriptions, Clash YAML, sing-box JSON and WireGuard config files are detected automatically.
source.content_placeholder: ss://… or vless://…, one per line; Clash YAML also works
source.delete_confirm: Delete “{name}”? Configs using it will report the missing source in check results.
source.kind_hint.batch: Paste share links, Clash YAML, sing-box JSON or a WireGuard config — one or many, detected automatically
source.not_fetched: The subscription hasn't been fetched yet. Click “Fetch now”.
source.url_hint: The server fetches this URL directly; the provider can see the server's outbound IP.
sources.granted_hint: Usable in your configs and kept in sync with the owner; you can’t view or edit them. If the owner revokes, configs using them drop those nodes automatically.
sources.privacy: Your nodes are encrypted in the database and hidden from administrators on this site; the code is open source for you to review.
sources.subtitle: Your node library: subscriptions and manually added nodes. Each config picks and orders them.
sources.title: Nodes
stats.fields_hint: Updated weekly; settings are ordered by it.
stats.probes_hint: Requests using invalid or reset config links, plus rate-limited ones. Repeated entries suggest probing; consider blocking these addresses at your reverse proxy.
stats.since_hint: Totals are kept permanently. Only counts are stored, never who; page reloads don't count.
stats.title: Statistics
summary.traffic_hint: Traffic reported by the subscription provider
templates.dropped: Skipped {n} node sources the template refers to that no longer exist
templates.how: Save a config as a template from More in the editor. The default template is preselected when you create a config.
templates.name: Template name
templates.save_desc: Saves everything in this config: nodes and how they are written, routing rules, proxy chains, core settings and direct YAML edits. New configs can start from it.
templates.set_default: Use as the default for new configs
templates.update_hint: Replaces the template's contents with this config; its name and description stay.

terms.gate_first_hint: This site now has terms of use. Read and agree to continue; your nodes, configs and subscription links are not affected.
terms.gate_updated: The terms of use have changed
terms.gate_updated_hint: Read and agree to the new version to continue. Subscription links keep updating in the meantime.
terms.title: Terms of Use
tokens.desc: Let scripts call the API, for example to refresh node sources on a schedule or read subscription stats. Tokens can only reach node sources, rule sources, configs, subscription links, short links and stats; they cannot change account settings such as your password or two-step verification.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.once_hint: You won’t be able to see it again; if you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
tokens.scope_hint: A token is as sensitive as a password: don’t commit it to a repository or share it. All tokens are revoked automatically when your password is recovered or reset by an administrator.
wizard.done_desc: Add the link to your client. You can refine everything in the editor later; the subscription updates automatically.
wizard.more_targets: For other clients, choose mihomo: it produces a standard mihomo config.
wizard.nodes_q: Where do your nodes come from?
wizard.rules_later_desc: Generate a config with nodes only for now.
